findings.chapter: Chapter 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: “At the canonical instance rate (~$20/hr per 8×H100 host), the canonical 6–21-host fleet on the owned/self-host basis is roughly $87.6K–$306.6K/month”
findings.issue: Cross-chapter cost-basis inconsistency. The $87.6K figure is the 6-host cloud paid-occupancy line and $306.6K is the 21-host cloud always-on line in the §4.3 sidebar (pages 70–72). The self-host 21-host line in that same sidebar is $155,816.93/month. Labeling the cloud range as “owned/self-host basis” contradicts the earlier table and misstates the cost basis.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace “owned/self-host basis” with the correct basis, e.g. “cloud paid-occupancy / cloud always-on basis,” or restate the self-host range using the $155,816.93 self-host 21-host line and the corresponding self-host 6-host line. Ensure the per-1K figures are also named to the matching basis.

findings.chapter: Chapter 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: “Self-host cost per million input-only / output-only tokens … ($120/hr whole-fleet at ~6 hosts) ÷ (92,000 input tok/s × 3600 s/hr) → ~$0.362/1M input …”
findings.issue: The cost-basis table labels the $120/hr whole-fleet calculation as “Self-host cost,” but $120/hr is six hosts at the $20/hr on-demand cloud rental price. In the same chapter, “self-host” is priced separately with capex amortization and energy ($155,816.93/month for 21 hosts). This is a provenance/cost-basis label mismatch that can mislead procurement comparisons.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the table row as “Cloud on-demand rental cost per million tokens” or recompute the row using the chapter’s self-host capex/energy basis. Do not use “self-host” for the $20/hr on-demand rental basis.

findings.evidence: "that occupancy and the canonical 8×H100 host definition are derived in Ch 4 §4.3 and Table 4-2"
findings.issue: Cross-reference "Ch 4 §4.3" violates the reading convention stated on p.19: "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." The reference repeats the chapter number 4 in "§4.3" after already naming "Ch 4". Under the stated convention, "Ch 4 §4.3" would parse as Chapter 4, Section 4, Subsection 3 (i.e. §4.4.3), which does not exist; the intended target is Section 3 (= "4.3. Worked Example").
findings.fix_instruction: Change "Ch 4 §4.3" to either "Ch 4 § 3" (chapter named, section stands alone) or "§4.3" (full form). Per the convention: "Ch. 7 § 3 means Ch. 7, Section 3" and "§ 7.3.1 is Ch. 7, Section 3, Subsection 1."

findings.chapter: Ch 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: "The minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline under the stated 35% MFU assumption is four, not eight: the 9.2K prefill is ≈1.29 PFLOP of work at 140 GFLOP/token, implying ≈1.19 PFLOPS of required compute rate over 1.08 s (9,200 × 140 GFLOP ÷ 1.08 s); one H100 sustains ~2,472 tok/s at 35% MFU, so a single GPU needs ~3.7 s for it (9,200 ÷ 2,472 = 3.72 s) and fails the cap, while ⌈1.19 PFLOPS ÷ (0.989 × 0.35)⌉ ≈ 4 GPUs meet it — the 8-GPU host needs ~0.47 s (9,200 ÷ 19,780 = 0.465 s)"
findings.issue: The 35% MFU planning value is used here to decide a hardware count ('the minimum GPU count ... is four'), but the Ch. 2 / Ch. 8 planning-MFU figure is explicitly a 'planning rate, not a ceiling' and the whole chapter labels analytical screens as 'not capacity results'. More seriously, the same paragraph's framing conflicts with the book's stated measurement discipline: Ch. 14 §14.4 and Ch. 8 require MFU to come from a benchmark, and the 35% figure is carried as [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]. A 'minimum GPU count ... is four' derived from an assumed MFU is presented in the same sentence as a measured-sounding conclusion, and the 'four' number then reappears in Ch. 4 §4.8's mini-case host-count discussion ('the minimum GPU count for this single-request prefill deadline ... is four, not eight') with the same status. The figure is analytically a lower bound (real MFU below 35% would require more), but the text states it as 'the minimum GPU count', which reads as a determined count.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-label the four-GPU figure as an analytical lower bound conditional on the assumed 35% MFU — e.g. 'at the stated 35% MFU planning assumption the prefill deadline needs ≥4 GPUs; real MFU below 35% raises that count, so this is a floor to verify by benchmark, not a determined count' — and carry the [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] MFU label with it wherever the 'four' recurs (Ch. 4 §4.8).

findings.chapter: Ch 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: "Reference: one 8×H100 host (the ~$15,000 row) ~$14.6K — 730 h/mo" versus the sidebar's "Self-host — 21-host peak KV-screen fleet $155,816.93 ... 21 × ($350K ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.3333 capex + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff"
findings.issue: The self-host energy term is stated as '$1,110.33' per host per month with no derivation anywhere in Ch. 4 or the visible Ch. 16 text, and the capex is stated as '$350K' per host with no source. These two numbers are the entire basis of the self-host line item ($155,816.93), which the chapter then converts into '$24.97 per 1K requests' and compares against the cloud lines. Neither the $350K capex nor the $1,110.33 energy figure carries an evidence label or a derivation; Ch. 16 is where the TCO is developed, but the figure as presented in Ch. 4 reads as a computed total from unlabelled inputs, against the book's own rule that 'every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair'.
findings.fix_instruction: Either move the self-host line out of Ch. 4 (leaving a pointer to Ch. 16) or attach the derivation and evidence labels for the $350K capex and the $1,110.33 energy term in place — stating the assumed PUE, host power draw, electricity price and amortisation horizon. If the values are canonical-scenario inputs, label them [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] and label the $155,816.93 total [canonical scenario][DERIVED].

findings.evidence: Page 113, Table 4-1 'Economic constraints' row: 'at the ~6-host average the whole-fleet spend is ~$120/hour ... giving ~2.76M input ... tokens per $1 of fleet spend (active-hours basis)'. Sidebar note below: 'The ~$15,000 budget line ... is an illustrative per-host cap'. Note †: 'The ~655K input-tokens-per-$1 alternative divides the $87,600 paid-for-730-h month... an hour-basis mismatch'.
findings.issue: Ambiguous Provenance / Basis Mismatch. The main table quotes '2.76M tokens/$' based on active-hours spend ($120/hr), while the sidebar quotes '$14.04/1K req' (which derives to ~71K tokens/$) based on 730-hour paid occupancy ($87,600/mo). Although explained in Note †, the juxtaposition of these widely different unit costs in the primary summary table vs the sidebar without immediate qualification risks misinterpretation of the 'Economic Constraints' baseline.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a footnote to the 'Economic constraints' cell in Table 4-1 explicitly stating that this is an 'Active-Hours Only' basis and is NOT comparable to standard cloud monthly TCO figures which include idle paid hours.
